chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to me from Ahmad b. Muhammad from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Abu Jamila from Jabir from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him).

He said: An angel from the angels passed by a man standing at the door of a house. The angel said to him: 'O servant of Allah, what makes you stand at the door of this house?' He said: 'A brother of mine is in it; I wanted to greet him.' The angel said: 'Is there close kinship between you and him, or did a need bring you to him?' He said: So he said: 'No, there is no kinship between us, nor did any need bring me to him — only the brotherhood of Islam and his sanctity. I pledge myself to him and greet him for the sake of Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.' The angel said: 'I am a messenger of Allah to you. He sends you His peace and says: It is only Me that you wanted, and it is to Me that you pledged. I have made Paradise obligatory for you, relieved you from My anger, and delivered you from the Fire.'

key_terms.أتعاهده: I pledge myself to him — maintaining ties and visiting
key_terms.أخوة الإسلام: Brotherhood of Islam — the spiritual bond uniting all believers
key_terms.الجنة: Paradise — the ultimate reward in the afterlife
key_terms.حرمة: Sanctity/inviolability — the sacred status of a fellow Muslim
key_terms.رحم ماسة: Close kinship — blood ties or immediate family

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting a Muslim brother solely for the sake of Allah according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) narrates a story in which an angel encounters a man visiting his Muslim brother purely for the sake of Allah — with no family ties or material need. God sends the angel as a messenger to tell the man that by visiting a fellow believer for Allah's sake, he has in fact sought Allah Himself. The reward is Paradise, protection from divine wrath, and deliverance from the Fire. This hadith powerfully establishes the spiritual merit of maintaining bonds of Islamic brotherhood (ukhuwwa) motivated solely by faith.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to me from Ahmad b. Muhammad from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Abi Jamila from Jabir from Abi Ja`far al-Baqir (as).

He said: An angel from the angels passed by a man standing at the door to a house. So, the angel said to him: “O servant of Allah! What brought you to the door of this house?” He said: “I have a brother in it, and I want to greet him.” So, the angel said: “Is he a part of your immediate family, or do you need something from him?” He said: So, he said: “No, we are not related, nor do I need anything from him – only the brotherhood of Islam and his sanctity [as a believer]. I [only wish to] pledge myself to him and greet him in [the name of] Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.” So, the angel said: “I am a messenger of Allah to you. He recites the salaam to you and says: ‘It is only I that you wanted [to greet], and I that you wanted to pledge to, so I have made Paradise obligatory for you, and I have relieved you from My anger, and I have delivered you from the Fire.’”
